James Milner – New York City Marathon 2026 – 3:09:04

So Milner’s time puts him above some pretty distinguished company, but there are five former footballers who have managed to go quicker.

The remaining five have all posted times that would be the envy of most amateur runners, with two even managing to break the elusive three-hour mark. There’s very little to separate the top four:

Not trying to step on Football Cliches‘ turf, but Christian Dailly is the name of a long-distance Olympian, not a Barclays-era stalwart. So this makes sense.

The former Scotland international had called time on a 22-year playing career in 2012, but wasn’t quite ready to put his sporting ambitions to bed. Instead, he turned his attention to athletics, becoming a coach and studying sports science at Manchester Metropolitan University.

In an interview with The Scotsman ahead of his first London Marathon in 2013, Dailly explained that he was more naturally suited to shorter, sharper events such as the 800m. He nevertheless had his sights set on a sub-three-hour marathon.

“You’re talking about someone who has had 22 years of football training and seven knee operations,” he said.

He ultimately finished in 3:06:26, just over six minutes outside his target. Not bad for a first attempt

You wouldn’t necessarily associate Grant with long-distance running, given he spent much of his career as a back-up, or latterly third-choice at Manchester United.

More accustomed to warming the bench than pounding the pavements? Apparently not.

Finishing just 33 seconds off the hallowed sub-three hours must’ve been a sickener, but at least he could console himself by comfortably beating Daddy Pig (5:51:53), Joe Wicks (5:51:54) and fellow journeyman keeper Darren Randolph (7:36:27).

A particularly impressive effort given the injury troubles that dogged his playing career. Ramsey completed the London Marathon in 3:00:30, three seconds quicker than Grant.

Only three celebrities went quicker: former Olympic cyclist Chris Newton (2:34:42), boxing trainer Shane McGuigan (2:44:51) and four-time F1 world champion Sebastian Vettel (2:59:08).

Ramsey retired from football the same month, aged 35, after a trophy-laden career with Arsenal, Juventus and Wales. He went straight into coaching, and is currently serving as the head coach of League One side Oxford United.

Dailly has the name of a marathon runner, Robben has the physique of one. He’s looked like a distance runner throughout his life, but even he admitted that 26.2 miles is a different proposition than sprinting up and down the wing.

“I am really broken, but I made it,” he told NOS after making the finish line.

“For a sprinter like me, such a distance is very long. But I love sports and I love a challenge.”

He had been training alongside former Dutch speed skater Erben Wennemars, who doubled up as his unofficial running coach and sports psychologist.

“Wennemars always says: once an athlete, always an athlete,” he added.

“I am no longer a top athlete, but I can tell you; I think it is elite sport if you can run a marathon in three hours.

“This comes very close to winning a great football title. Now I can check this off. I’m really happy.”

There are people who enjoy keeping fit, and then there’s Luis Enrique. The PSG manager is an absolute endurance nut, seemingly incapable of encountering a physical challenge without wanting to go all-in. Long-distance cycling is a particular passion, but he’s not afraid of mixing things up.

He competed in the notorious Marathon des Sables in 2008, running 155km across the Sahara over six days, and has also completed the Frankfurt Ironman: a 3.8km swim, 189km cycle and 42.2km marathon.

You’d imagine a sub-three-hour marathon barely registers on Luis Enrique’s personal difficulty scale. We’d have been disappointed if he hadn’t topped this particular leaderboard.

It’s an attitude that carries over into his coaching. Luis Enrique is famously demanding, expecting his players to push themselves to their physical and mental limits. His PSG side have won back-to-back European titles by embodying precisely those principles, with every player expected to work hard, sacrifice and run their b*llocks off.

#1485. Emiliano Martinez reveals his finger 'won't ever return' to normal after injury left him playing like a 'zombie' during World Cup: 'I cried every day'

Published: 19:19 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 19:33 EDT, 30 October 2026

Emiliano Martinez has revealed his finger will never return to normal after he played through injury to represent Argentina at the World Cup.

Martinez broke and dislocated a finger in the warm-up before playing for Aston Villa in their Europa League final triumph over Freiburg in May.

The 34-year-old told Argentine journalist Gaston Edul’s YouTube channel that he cried after seeing x-rays having feared he would be ruled out of Argentina's World Cup title defence.

After receiving support from Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni, Martinez explained a decision was taken to avoid undergoing surgery that would have ruled him out of the tournament.

Martinez was instead provided with a special glove from Adidas to protect the injured finger, which he admitted meant he could not grasp the ball properly.

'It will never go back to how it was,' Martinez said. 'I am still playing with pain.'

Emiliano Martinez has revealed his finger will never return to normal after he played through injury to represent Argentina at the World Cup. Source: YouTube/Gastón Edul

Martinez sustained a broken finger before playing for Aston Villa in the Europa League final

The shot stopper wore a special glove from Adidas to protect his injured finger to ensure he could play at the World Cup, but admits he will need surgery in the future

'The day before Algeria I was diving with one arm, diving like a zombie.

'If I put my hand down I was seeing stars. It was brutal. Every single night I was crying because my finger looked like a sausage.

'But these are the risks you take for the national team, I’d do it again.'

Martinez added that a summer transfer to Italy – with Juventus having targeted the star – ultimately collapsed as a direct result of the injury.

'I got an x-ray and it was broken again,' Martinez said. 'That is when a transfer to a club fell through because of the finger.

'They said it was possible for me to play like that, that I needed surgery, but Chelsea didn't, they didn't care. One day I will need surgery.'

Martinez, who joined Chelsea for £7.5million in the summer, is currently recovering from a broken jaw sustained in their victory over Everton earlier this month.

#1484. Spurs finally score... but still lose

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”

Rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo said.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc

"They've done themselves proud!" 👏Conor Coady on Lewis Koumas performance for Liverpool 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3JGkuY7Eye

The visitors take advantage of very poor keeping from Mamardashvili. Fernandes’ delivery should be dealt with by Mamardashvili but the Georgian keeper flaps at empty air. It comes to Gallagher, who has a simple header from just a few yards out. A lifeline for Tottenham, who have their first goal this season against Premier League opposition.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

Tottenham have had some decent chances tonight. The latest comes for Gallagher just inside the Liverpool box but his effort takes a deflection off Kerkez and goes behind for a corner...

That is a crucial challenge from Kerkez inside his own box. Marmoush looked like he was going to have a great opportunity from 10 yards out in the centre of Liverpool’s penalty area but Kerkez intervenes with a superbly-timed challenge to deny the Egyptian.

Double change for Liverpool as Szoboszlai and Gravenberch replace Nyoni and McConnell in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield.

Mamardashvili makes an important save. Marmoush carries the ball a long way down Tottenham’s left before cutting inside. As he gets to the Liverpool box, he plays the ball across to his right to find Kudus, whose first-time effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his left.

Robertson is going to come on for Tottenham against his former side and receives a great reception from the Liverpool fans, similarly to the reception Ray Clemence received all those years ago:

Legendary goalkeeper, Ray Clemence would've turned 78 today ❤️Not many former players get a reception as good as this when they come back to Anfield, he was a true Liverpool great 🙌 pic.twitter.com/NLH3nZUJjd

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Tosin decides to shoot from range but drags his effort wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

The home side double their lead at The Kop end. Kerkez perhaps should shoot from the edge of the box but instead lays it back to Mac Allister. The Argentine then plays it to his left to find Gakpo, who cuts inside onto his right and fires into the far corner. This now his tenth goal in 13 League Cup appearances.

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

No chances to speak of in the early stages of this second half.

We are back under way at Anfield. Liverpool have made a change at the break with Jacquet coming on for Gomez. This was Gomez’s first game back after injury.

Possession: Liverpool 47%-53% TottenhamShots: 6-6Shots on target: 2-1Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 10-8

Tottenham did have two big chances through Bergvall and Kudus and there are arguments to say both of them should have scored.

Mac Allister takes but his effort is off target. That is indeed the final moment of the half and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of that fine Mac Allister strike.

We are past the two initial minutes added on but that is because of the delay when Senesi was given a talking-to moments ago. That allows Liverpool to win a free-kick not far outside the Tottenham box and Bentancur is booked for the foul on Gakpo.

This will be the final moment of the half.

Senesi absolutely clatters into McConnell but somehow escapes without a booking. There have been a number of soft yellows in this first yet one of the most blatant yellows is not given as a booking.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Marmoush is the first Tottenham player booked tonight for a foul on McConnell and that feels on the harsh side. Definitely a foul but was it a yellow?

That is a dreadful decision from referee Andy Madley. Frimpong gets the better of Tel in a contest down Tottenham’s left, with the former outmuscling the latter. Not only is Frimpong penalised, he is booked.

Mac Allister spurns a glorious chance to get his and Liverpool’s second of the night. Tottenham again risk it at the back and lose it. McConnell then feeds a pass into the box to pick out the run of Koumas, who squares it for Mac Allister. The Argentine cannot get his feet sorted in time and wastes the opportunity from eight yards out.

Liverpool want a penalty. Tottenham give it away cheaply inside their own box and McConnell goes down under a challenge from Senesi, who was the one who gave it away. It was a clumsy challenge from Senesi and if VAR was in action tonight it would have been interesting to see what they would have done with that as Senesi did barge into the back of McConnell.

Araujo is then booked for pulling Marmoush back.

There is no way Tottenham’s goal drought will last in perpetuity but they have missed two fabulous chances so far and you wonder what impact that will have on their confidence. At least one Tottenham player is being feted: Andy Robertson, who has just jogged down the touchline at Anfield in a different kit for the first time in nine years. He tried not to acknowledge the singing of his name too much but you could see it meant something to him.

The home fans serenade their former player Robertson as the now Tottenham left-back goes out to warm up.

That is a big chance for Kudus to equalise on the counter. Tottenham break from deep inside their own half and charge down their left. Bergvall waits for Udogie to come on the overlap before playing the pass. From the left side of the box, Udogie crosses for Kudus, who gets across the front of Kerkez. Kudus should probably score but lifts his effort over the bar from just six yards out.

What a goal......that would of been! 🫢Kudus fires over what would of been a sensational move from Spurs#ITVFootball | @Carabao_Cup pic.twitter.com/a1TPzKyJlP

Gomez gives the ball away cheaply inside his own half before McConnell is penalised for a foul on Marmoush. Will Tottenham cross it or take the shot on from around 25 yards out? The answer is the latter and Marmoush goes for goal but misses the target.

That was a chance for Udogie. Senesi clips in a lovely ball over the top in behind to pick out the run from left-back of Udogie, who tries to chest it down but cannot keep it under control. Had he done so, it would have been a great chance.

The way Alexis Mac Allister has played this past fortnight, anyone would think he is trying to secure himself a new contract. All cynicism aside, that was a quite beautiful goal and attention must be drawn to Cody Gakpo’s involvement: he took a pass on his chest from Joe Gomez before opening up the pitch. We will say it again: the idea of selling Gakpo in the last window was madness.

He scored a stunner nearly a week ago against Atletico Madrid here in the Champions League and he adds another storming strike to his repertoire. The ball finds kindly to Mac Allister on the edge of the box after Udogie tackled Ngumoha and the Argentine finds the top corner with a first-time finish.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Koumas comes close to putting Liverpool in front with their first real chance of the game. Ngumoha slides a clinical pass into the box to pick out the run in behind of Koumas, who gets the better of Senesi. Koumas takes a great first touch before getting his shot away but is denied by Dubravka. Both goalkeepers have now been forced into good saves early doors.

Close for Lewis Koumas!The Liverpool youngster is denied by Martin Dubravka after some brilliant play by Rio Ngumoha 🪄 pic.twitter.com/YNC8QEAGGG

Given their team has been bang average this season, the huge number of travelling Spurs fans are making a magnificent noise. They could have celebrated a long-overdue goal had it not been for a magnificent save by Giorgi Mamardashvili. The Georgian needed to make it from Lucas Bergvall, as a minute beforehand he dithered while Joe Gomez was shepherding a ball back to him and those on the Kop lost their minds. It’s tense amongst Liverpool supporters. You wonder how it changes.

That is a fantastic save from Mamardashvili. Gallagher plays the ball to Udogie on the left side of the box and the latter squares it to Bergvall in the centre of the box. Bergvall is no more than eight yards out and must think he is going to score but Mamardashvili makes a great save to deny the Swede. Should Bergvall have given Mamardashvili the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

Tottenham are dominating possession thus far, with a lot of the game being played in Liverpool’s half at the moment.

The heavens have well and truly opened at Anfield, with the rain heaving down.

Tottenham win a corner off Gomez out on the right. Kudus clips in an inswinger that Araujo heads away.

Gakpo is starting out on the left for Liverpool tonight, with Ngumoha on the right and Koumas leading the line down the centre. Gakpo was linked with a move to Tottenham and Manchester City over the summer but stayed at Liverpool.

Tottenham have a free-kick not far outside the Liverpool penalty area on the right as Kerkez is penalised for blocking Gallagher’s cross with his arm. Kudus’ delivery is headed away by Araujo.

Kudus keeps it alive and sends in another cross that ends up in Mamardashvili’s arms.

We are under way at Anfield, with a place in the fourth round at stake.

A reminder, there is no extra time so it the game is all square after 90 minutes we will go straight to penalties. Also, there is no VAR tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. In Virgil van Dijk’s absence, Joe Gomez captains Liverpool tonight. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Let's get to work 💪 pic.twitter.com/ji1hsS4tyt

Andrew Robertson played nearly 400 games for Liverpool and won countless trophies with the club, including two Premier League titles, two League Cups and the Champions League. Upon his return to Anfield, he starts on the bench against his former employers.

Djaksparo is a rising musician from Paris who who gained viral fame following a social media boost from Liverpool’s summer signing Bradley Barcola, who is on the bench for the hosts this evening.

Welcome to Anfield, Djaksparo 👋 pic.twitter.com/iueYa1KjL7

"I would like to see the goals!"Roberto De Zerbi ahead of Spurs clash with Liverpool in the Carabao Cup 🙌 pic.twitter.com/uSjCJcnAfJ

Richarlison is not happy at Roberto de Zerbi's decision to leave him out of Tottenham's squad tonight 🙅‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/WqRWb3KPed

“There is no joy watching Spurs at the moment. Last year was a survival job, but now you have got to flip it. [Roberto] De Zerbi’s got a lot of players at his disposal.

“He has got to fit that jigsaw puzzle together. There are still a lot of elements that are not right; they have not got a left-sided player they can trust in. Goals have been a real problem, but I do think they will come.”

During the Spaniard’s three seasons at the helm at Bournemouth, he never made it past the fourth round in this competition. He reached the fourth round in his first season at Bournemouth during the 2023/24 season but in the last two seasons has fallen in the second round, which was the round Bournemouth entered the competition.

Just one player remains from Liverpool’s starting XI against Fulham on Saturday and that is Ronald Araujo. Virgil van Dijk and Florian Wirtz are given the night off for the home side.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili, Frimpong, Araujo, Gomez, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Nyoni, McConnell, Ngumoha, Koumas, Gakpo.Substitutes: Alisson, Endo, Jacquet, Szoboszlai, Isak, Munoz, Barcola, Gravenberch, Chambers.

Roberto De Zerbi makes eight changes from Tottenham’s draw against Everton, with Archie Gray, Rodrigo Bentancur and Omar Marmoush the three players to remain in the starting XI.

Tottenham: Dubravka; Gray, Tosin, Senesi, Udogie; Bentancur, Bergvall; Kudus, Gallagher, Tel; Marmoush.Substitutes: Kinsky, Robertson, Van Hecke, Maddison, Savio, Fernandes, Solanke, Davies, Van de Ven.

We're in the building 🏟️ pic.twitter.com/nPJefN5F3A

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

Peterborough vs Barnsley 7.30pmWest Ham vs Fulham 7.45pmIpswich vs Arsenal 8pmLiverpool vs Tottenham 8pmReading vs Brentford 8pm

Our Spurs side to take on Liverpool 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/X4f3F0cl4f

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1483. Why Burnley gambled on Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss inspired by Che Guevara who boxes, dances and was an electrical engineer, to spark their season back to life - and why his new players are already worried about him

Published: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026

Not many football managers have a tattoo of Che Guevara, dance in their free time and speak five languages.

But they are just three quirks which add to the layers of intrigue around Burnley's new boss Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss tasked with saving the Clarets from double relegation and dropping into the third tier for the first time since 2000.

After four wins in the last year, with morale in the gutter, Burnley announced Celestini as Nicky Hayen's successor on Wednesday. Many fans will have dropped their marmalade. Who? Celestini's CV is promising but this is an almighty gamble and they cannot afford for things to go wrong.

The Clarets sit 22nd in the Championship and have won just one home game inside 90 minutes in 2026. Their summer was an unmitigated disaster – they had woeful pre-season results, went 71 days without a manager, sold last campaign's top scorer Zian Flemming on deadline day with no replacement, and their chief executive, James Holroyd, walked out in September after difficulties working alongside chairman Alan Pace.

The club is in £142million of debt, according to their latest accounts, with £13m in cash in the coffers. The phrase 'basket case' comes to mind.

Celestini's appointment falls squarely on the shoulders of new chief football officer Diego Lopez, another stranger to English football, and it is one Burnley's players are unsure about.

Fabio Celestini is facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation with Burnley, who sit 22nd in the Championship

Belgian boss Nicky Hayen lasted just 12 league matches - and won only once

Burnley have not been in the third tier since 2000 but are staring down the barrel of a second successive relegation

Daily Mail Sport understands that some members of the squad have reservations about Celestini's style of play – he has favoured a possession-based 4-2-3-1 throughout his career, a system which Hayen tried and failed to implement during his time in charge.

Many clubs have turned to outsiders and succeeded – just look at table-toppers Middlesbrough under Kim Hellberg – but the lack of Championship experience in Burnley's management structure leaves Celestini to navigate a steep learning curve without much support.

On the bright side, Celestini inherited a similarly shambolic case at Basel in October 2023 and thrived. The Swiss giants were bottom of the table and had had to cancel their goal of the month award, because they hadn't scored any. Celestini saved them from relegation, restored the feel-good factor by re-signing club legend Xherdan Shaqiri, and won them the league and cup double the following season.

The 50-year-old former Switzerland midfielder – who won 35 caps for his country and played against England's Golden Generation at Euro 2004 – also has a promotion on his ledger from his time at Lausanne and a Swiss Cup with Luzern. He also led Lugano into Europe and managed Sion.

'Celestini is a determined, ambitious personality, but he can also be a stubborn coach and that has caused issues at several clubs,' Swiss football expert Craig King (@FootballSwissEN on X) tells Daily Mail Sport.

'He is capable of providing clubs with a short-term bounce before it eventually deteriorates. He has strong ideas, but his stubbornness often tends to rub people the wrong way.

'It seems that inevitably, he loses control of his teams somewhere along the way and can never get them back on track.'

His time at Russian giants CSKA Moscow, last season after he left Basel, followed that trend.  He had found out about their interest on a holiday with his dancer wife, Fanny, in the Seychelles, and took the plunge, rocking up with a Spanish-speaking coaching coterie. He even appointed his wife to help edit video clips for analysis and support in aspects of communication, a club source tells Daily Mail Sport.

He enjoyed a strong start at CSKA – he won the Russian Super Cup in his first match and they led the Russian Premier League after 11 games. Going into the winter break, they were just four points off top in fourth.

'Fabio has done a tremendous job,' the club's general director Roman Babaev said during that hiatus. 'There was beautiful football.'

By the end of Celestini's tenure in May, Babaev was describing a 'lack of self-confidence and a lack of belief in their ability to turn the situation around'. He added: 'We agreed that things could only get worse – the head coach doubted the team was listening to him.'

Celestini won 35 caps for Switzerland and appeared against England at Euro 2004

Burnley are Celestini's eighth club as a manager, having left CSKA Moscow by mutual consent in May

What changed? Reports in Russia claimed that over the winter break, players had been unimpressed with the lack of physical and defensive work, with too much emphasis on attacking and set-pieces. They lost their first three games back after the break, suffered a humbling 4-0 thrashing by Krasnodar in the Russian Cup, and went winless in Celestini's final five matches in charge.

In the space of two months, everything had unravelled. After defender Moises was sent off in the drubbing at Krasnodar, Celestini reprimanded the player in the dressing room – but the Brazilian hit back, questioning his manager's competence in front of the team. Moises was subsequently suspended and the club took Celestini's side.

'I felt like something was missing, I wasn't feeling well, something wasn't right. Other players started saying they weren't feeling well,' Moises later reflected in the documentary We Are CSKA. 'To become a champion, you need to cleanse yourself of all dirt. I blurted it all out because I knew what was simmering inside us all.'

Celestini is still well thought of at CSKA and was always willing to take accountability rather than criticise his players publicly. Former manager Viktor Goncharenko claimed that he ultimately failed because he 'didn't find common ground with the CSKA veterans', such as legendary goalkeeper Igor Akinfeev, and didn't have enough Russian coaches. He left with the club sixth in the table.

Celestini's task now is to turn around a flailing Burnley. His first assignment will be on Saturday at Turf Moor against in-form Portsmouth. Based off how he describes himself, he does not come across as a disciplinarian. Celestini says he does not like implementing fines and is not a fan of throwing things across a dressing room.

'This kind of half-time behavior might only work once a season,' he once said. 'It's like an electric shock.'

At his heart Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana.

His tattoo of Cuban revolutionary Guevara cost 180 Swiss francs (£163). He has lost count of his tattoos by now, also inking his kids and a depiction of good triumphing over evil.

Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana

Daily Mail Sport understands some Burnley players have reservations about Celestini's possession-based 4-2-3-1, a system which Hayen failed to implement

'I started reading about (Guevara), studying him. My tattoo depicts him without his military beret. There are no political references,' he said. 'What attracts me to him is that he fought his whole life for those who had nothing to do with him, and I've also fought a lot in my life, so I decided to get it.'

Another of his heroes is Nelson Mandela: 'He also dedicated his entire life to his ideas. Anyone who fought for their ideals is important to me. I admire people who take the time to help others. I don’t consider myself a good person, but I’m not a hypocrite.'

Away from football, Celestini – who speaks Italian, French, Spanish, German and English – also dances with his wife and enjoys boxing. A former electrical draughtsman, he has a good work ethic and, we hear, made a strong push for the Burnley job.

A source at the Clarets, who were also interested in Rob Edwards and Carlos Corberan, insists that Celestini was their first choice. Now they are counting on him to deliver a minor miracle.

#1482. Meet the Premier League's most-wanted boss on the rise: Fabian Hurzeler, 33, has Brighton flying after eventful summer - including SECOND hair transplant and secret wedding to actress girlfriend

Published: 03:01 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 03:01 EDT, 31 October 2026

After replacing the combustible - but effective - Roberto De Zerbi in the summer of 2024, Brighton appeared to have selected his opposite in then-31-year-old Fabian Hurzeler.

The German arrived from helping St Pauli achieve promotion to the Bundesliga with big shoes to fill, with De Zerbi's Brighton frequently punching above their weight with their free-flowing, front-footed style. And aside from his multiple tattoos, which span the length of both arms, his chest, and his stomach, little about Hurzeler shouted.

Hurzeler has largely kept his head down and focused on imprinting his message on his players. The rewards have been quietly impressive, with back-to-back eighth-place Premier League finishes. But at the start of this 2026-27 season, the 33-year-old German manager has taken the side to the next level with the Seagulls justifiably perched in third place at the start of this game weekend.

The road there has been paved with some eye-popping results, with the free-scoring, free-wheeling side scoring four past Aston Villa, five against Crystal Palace, and three to stun the Premier League champions Arsenal, all without reply.

There have been bumps in the road, in the form of defeat to Liverpool clicking into gear under Andoni Iraola, a recent lacklustre turn in the Europa Conference League against Czech minnows Jablonec and being knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Manchester City on penalties just three days ago. But the latter can be avenged quickly, with Brighton returning to the Etihad in league action on Saturday afternoon.

Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at Hurzeler's transformational summer ahead of what could be the strongest season of his spell at Brighton - and what happens when league rivals start eyeing him to takeover at bigger sides.

Fabian Hurzeler has overseen a promising start to the season on the south coast with Brighton

The heavily tattooed manager has grown in stature since arriving at the club in 2024 (Source: Instagram/Fabian Hurzeler)

Brighton's rise comes after an eventful summer for Hurzeler, which included going public with his now-wife Anna Karolin Berger (Source: Instagram/Anna Karolin Berger)

While many involved in international football took in this summer's World Cup as fans, Hurzeler had a singularly unique experience alongside his own break Stateside after connecting with Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti.

The legendary Don Carlo has helmed international giants including Real Madrid, AC Milan, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, but working with Brazil in North American represented his first international tournament experience with a national team.

Hurzeler and Ancelotti were put in touch by the iconic manager's son Davide, who is also finding his way in management, and spoke at length over Zoom, where, Hurzeler told the Athletic, he was invited to join Brazil's World Cup camp.

While the finer details of the schedule kept Hurzeler from attending training, the duo did meet at Ancelotti's hotel, with Ancelotti sharing yet more valuable nuggets with the young manager.

'The funny thing was, we watched England against Croatia together,' he said. 'We just talked about football. He shared a few stories.

'For example, Luka Modric was on the pitch. He shared some stories about Modric, how he was, how he acted as a leader.'

While travelling across the United States and taking in games both as a fan of his native Germany, and on analysis duty for talkSPORT, Hurzeler had a companion. German actress Anna Karolin Berger went public with her boyfriend in a sweet snap taken at Germany's win against Ivory Coast in Toronto, with the 34-year-old posting a picture with Hurzeler from the stands.

The soap star actress currently appears in long-running serial Sturm der Liebe (Storm of Love), and in light of her similarly high profile, both she and Hurzeler had previously kept their romance under wraps.

After sharing Hurzeler to her Instagram account in June however, the floodgates of public appearances opened, with Berger sharing pictures of the couple holidaying in Mauritius, taking in a Formula One raceday, and even posing at Brighton's home ground.

Berger shared a photo in August of her in attendance at the Amex for Brighton's season-opening Premier League match, a 4-0 victory over Aston Villa.

The 34-year-old is a soap actress in her native Germany and appears on a popular serial

In August, Berger - who is based in Munich - posed at the Amex for Brighton's first home game

Since they first announced their relationship the couple are believed to have got married

The actress captioned the image: 'no worries - I’m a keeper.'

But rather than a recent romance, Hurzeler and Berger had most likely kept shtum for some time, with the manager seemingly returning from the late-summer international break a married man.

Hurzeler was spotted wearing a wedding ring when the action returned after the three-week hiatus. But neither Berger nor Hurzeler has publicly confirmed the happy news - yet.

Summer also allowed for a physical transformation for Hurzeler, although not his first. Shortly after his move to the Premier League in 2024, the former St Pauli manager joked on BILD's Phrasenmaher podcast that his primary similarity to fellow German manager Jurgen Klopp was that 'we both had our hair enhanced a bit'.

But ahead of the start of this season, Hurzeler may have wanted another enhancement, with the manager appearing on the sidelines of Brighton's pre-season clash with Roma sporting a freshly shaven head.

Fans speculated online as to whether Hurzeler might have returned for a second transplant, or merely removed his toupee - with the head coach understandably never confronting their theories directly.

Nearly four months on however, Hurzeler is back to his more-recognisable brown short-back-and-sides crop.

The summer also seemingly saw Hurzeler undergo what might be his second hair transplant (left, in early August and right, on Wednesday)

As with any rising managerial prospect toiling at one of the Premier League's smaller clubs, as Hurzeler's side have grown in stature, so have rumours connecting him to some of the top flight's big beasts.

On the heels of the first transformational manager of Tony Bloom's tenure, Graham Potter, being pinched by Chelsea, Brighton's owner has been realistic about his chances of holding onto Hurzeler long-term.

'There are a lot of things one can worry about in the world, but losing a head coach or players is not one of them,' Bloom told the Athletic.

'Obviously, you really don't want to, but head coaches come and go, players come and go, but the football club is the one certain thing which will be here, hopefully, forever. So, there's no point thinking about these things.

'I think Fabian is very happy at the club; we're very happy with him, so long may that continue.

'I'm a very good sleeper. When I'm tired, I sleep. So I don't worry about these things. When there's a bad spell (of results), I still sleep well.'

Most recently, the loudest rumours have come from connections to crisis-struck Manchester United.

Although Michael Carrick remains at the helm for now, after a woeful start, members of the club's hierarchy have met to discuss the head coach's future, with results in desperate need of an uptick for him to cling onto his job past the upcoming international break.

Brighton have been among the clubs to hand Carrick's outfit a drubbing, with the Seagulls knocking the fallen giants out of the Carabao Cup on their first outing.

But should Man United wish to bet big on the league's hottest property, Brighton would likely slap a hefty price tag on their prodigal head coach, with Daily Mail Sport reporting that it could cost the Manchester club around £20million to prise him loose.

Nor might Hurzeler go willingly. As Bloom has stressed, the manager appears at home on the south coast, and he has just been treated to a bumper transfer window - with Brighton breaking their transfer record to lure talented young defender Luka Vuskovic from Tottenham.

Plus, Brighton sit a staggering 14 places above Man United in the Premier League table. With history-making Champions League football in their sights, Hurzeler might be forgiven for thinking he has the more tempting season ahead of him if he stays where he is.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

“We take it how it is. For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”

#1480. Revealed: SIX Man United stars named in combined XI with Chelsea despite Michael Carrick's side's nightmare start - as stats boffins pick Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans over Moises Caicedo

Published: 03:01 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EDT, 31 October 2026

As matchweek nine of this enthralling Premier League season rolls around we have a host of excellent games to look forward to this weekend.

Champions Arsenal will look to bounce back after a humiliating defeat away to Fleetwood in midweek but will have to travel to Anfield and take on a Liverpool side who look to have finally hit form, winning their last five games in all competitions.

Manchester City welcome third place Brighton, who have been the surprise package of the season so far. There is a London derby as Tottenham take on Crystal Palace.

Perhaps the most anticipated game is the 12:30 Saturday kick off between old rivals Chelsea and Manchester United.

The once perennial title challengers both find themselves struggling so far this season, albeit United much more so, and will be desperate to pick up three points.

Sofascore have put together a combined XI of the best-performing players from both squads, with average ratings accrued from all competitions this campaign. So, who has made the cut? Daily Mail Sport takes a look.

Between the sticks is Manchester United's big Belgian, Senne Lammens. The 24-year-old has been a breath of fresh air at Old Trafford after United after the struggles of his predecessor Andre Onana.

Onana who had some memorably poor performances in both the Champions League and Premier League during his two year spell in Manchester.

Lammens appears to have dropped off in form slightly from the end of last season but has still been solid considering his club's shocking form.

He gets the nod ahead of his Belgian compatriot Mike Penders who has had a tricky first few games in blue, and Emi Martinez who is still sidelined with a head injury he sustained away at Everton.

Senne Lammens is yet to keep a clean sheet in the Premier League this season as United have conceded 13 goals already

The first of our three central defenders is Chelsea's £70million man, Wesley Fofana.

A big-money signing from Leicester City in 2022, Fofana has only really begun to make regular appearances for Chelsea in the past year and has been a fixture when fit in Xabi Alonso's back-three system, starting all four games he has played.

Despite a number of lacklustre performances, most recently a nightmare at Anfield in midweek, overall the Frenchman has looked solid, winning 66 per cent of his defensive duels and 70 per cent of his aerial battles.

Playing through the middle of our back three is Harry Maguire.

Nobody in Manchester United's leaky defence has truly shone this season with the Red Devils already conceding 13 goals in the Premier League and six in the Champions League.

Nevertheless Maguire makes the cut, partially due to both sides not having performed at the back this season. Maguire has improved in possession hugely, registering a 90 per cent pass completion rate and a 100 per cent dribble success score.

Lisandro Martinez completes our defence despite his recent controversy.

Earlier this month Martinez found himself in hot water after making some serious criticism of Manchester United's transfer business - or lack of - and sporting director Jason Wilcox, but his personal performances have remained steady.

The Argentine scored a freakish own-goal away to Fulham in a 1-1 draw in September but has for the most part avoided any major errors at the back and certainly cannot be blamed for United's catastrophic start to the season.

When veteran Jordan Henderson was brought in over the summer many fans assumed he would play a bit-part role. Instead, the 36-year-old has become a regular starter for Alonso's team.

The Englishman has started every game for Chelsea since making his debut against Brentford and has been excellent, especially at home to Bournemouth in which he bagged a brace in a rampant 5-1 win.

Questions will be asked over whether he will be able to sustain this form over the course of the season given his age but for now he makes it into our XI with the highest average rating out of the lot.

The former Liverpool skipper as been a revelation at the Bridge this season, the only question is whether he keeps it up

Partnering Henderson is another Englishman who has rediscovered form this season but under different circumstances.

After a period out of favour with ex-manager Ruben Amorim, Kobbie Mainoo became the catalyst in his side's stellar end to last season. But this campaign his lack of ‘dynamism’ has been criticised by former player and now pundit Gary Neville.

Many have questioned if a midfield two of Mainoo and Youri Tielemans is sustainable due to the pair having similar profiles, and a combination of Mainoo and Carlos Baleba lacks experience.

Carrick has stuck with Mainoo thus far and individually he has earned solid ratings. He beats out Chelsea's Moises Caicedo to a place in the XI.

Pedro Neto has transformed his game under his new gaffer as an auxiliary wing-back.

The Portuguese has enjoyed his best start to a season at Chelsea since he joined the club for £65m back in 2024, scoring four and assisting one in eight games for the Blues so far.

He has also looked capable defensively in his new wing-back role in Chelsea's 3-4-2-1 formation with 55 defensive contributions and 29 ball recoveries this season.

If some places in this team are close calls, there is no questioning this man's inclusion. The Blues' £117m summer acquisition has so far looked worth every penny, lighting up the Premier League as one third of Chelsea's deadly front three.

The England star has five goals and has provided five assists in all competitions this campaign and appears to be that final piece of quality Chelsea have so desperately needed in attack.

Rogers has enjoyed a number of particularly memorable performances including his relentless showing at home to Leeds, where he assisted four goals, as well as his outing against Bournemouth in which he ran the game for 80 minutes and scored one.

Best friends Morgan Rogers (right) and Cole Palmer (left) also make the combined XI

At the beginning of the season, Bruno Fernandes would have been nailed on for this combined XI.

Just 12 games in, his inclusion may surprise a few. There is no questioning the man's ability but there have been serious concerns over whether his actions reflect what is expected of a United captain.

Fernandes has been very outspoken about the state of the club and the management of the squad and has subsequently had 'clear-the-air' talks with his boss.

The Portuguese international remains, however, one of the most talented midfielders in the Premier League and even with all of his issues off the pitch, he continues to contribute on it with four goals and one assist in all competitions.

Bruno Fernandes was benched for United's 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth but is back in for Saturday's visit to Chelsea

One has to feel a bit for Youri Tielemans. As a top talent entering the twilight of his career he has walked into an absolute car crash at Old Trafford.

And he has gone from a stellar season getting Champions League football with Aston Villa to sixteenth place with United in October. He is yet to wow the Stretford End.

Similarly to Kobbie Mainoo, the midfielder has been critiqued for his lack of running, with United sat third from bottom in the rankings when it comes to ground covered.

All the same, he has registered 371 passes - well above the league average - and has a completion rate of 89 per cent.

It is safe to say we are unlikely to see Palmer play up front this season but to fit the Blues' talisman in we have had to put him up top.

With Palmer fresh off the back of his first red card in senior football in Chelsea's 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham, it is easy to forget the start the Englishman has had to this campaign.

Seemingly energised after his omission from England's World Cup squad, the forward has looked back to his best at times.

He has racked up four goals and three assists so far and will be desperate to make an impact on his return from suspension against his boyhood club.

Sofascore's combined XI for this the grudge match of the weekend

#1479. Cole Palmer and Man United unpacked: The truth about Old Trafford links, why he really got a new Chelsea deal, Xabi Alonso's 'emotional control' advice after red card and how he must step up against 'Big Six' rivals

Published: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 05:46 EDT, 31 October 2026

Despite the speculation snowballing in the second half of last season – and it was as if there had been an explosion at a rumour mill – Manchester United never did come in for Cole Palmer.

No conversations were held with Chelsea in the summer. Not about him, anyway. United negotiated for Andrey Santos. It took two days to agree that deal, worth £48million plus £2m in easily achievable bonuses and with Chelsea retaining a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

But according to sources with knowledge of those talks and any others which occurred in that window, Palmer’s name was not mentioned whenever officials from both clubs, such as Chelsea sporting director, Paul Winstanley, and United director of football, Jason Wilcox, spoke.

Which might surprise a few. Because it was said Manchester United wanted Cole Palmer and Cole Palmer wanted Manchester United. Apparently he missed Manchester, could no longer stand London, was tired of waiting for Chelsea to be good again and thought he belonged in the Champions League. He was the boyhood United fan who grew up worshipping Wayne Rooney.

That was what we were seeing while scrolling social media in the build-up to a summer when England manager Thomas Tuchel excluded the 24-year-old from his World Cup squad.

In fairness, the original suggestion that Palmer might be interested in United was not plucked out of thin air. It is said that at least one person close to Palmer's circle was happy to stand up those suggestions.

Cole Palmer returns from suspension for Saturday's match against Manchester United, the club he was linked with in the summer

Palmer's red card against Tottenham last weekend was the first of his career

Daily Mail Sport has also learned one former United legend who dabbles in media work was likewise privately claiming he knew Palmer fancied the move. This came at a time when it was unclear whether Bruno Fernandes would be staying or sold to Saudi Arabia.

Yet nothing happened, and now, tomorrow at Stamford Bridge, Fernandes will return from the naughty step to represent United, and Palmer from his one-game suspension to play for Chelsea.

Chelsea had insisted all along that Palmer was untouchable. They even handed him another improved contract earlier this month, despite his last season not reaching the standards he had set for himself.

He ended an injury-interrupted 2025-26 with 11 goal involvements in the Premier League, after securing 23 in the previous season, and 33 before that.

When asked for the reasoning behind that new deal – whether it followed interest in him from a rival or was to provide parity after the £117million signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa – Chelsea sources described it as a desire to lock down one of their best players.

He was already contracted to 2033. Now he is tied to 2034 on a nicer salary. Nobody in the Premier League has a longer contract, though as Chelsea head into another challenging game against a ‘Big Six’ side, Palmer could do with earning his pay rise.

We have seen this playmaker step up on occasion, usually when there is a trophy for winning.

Palmer signed an improved contract at Chelsea earlier this month despite a below-par campaign last season

In the 2025 Club World Cup final, where he made Paris Saint-Germain’s superstars seem mediocre compared to him. In the Conference League final of that same year, where Palmer had a ‘sod it’ moment as he turned on his creativity, telling us afterwards that he was sick of going backwards and sideways, as per Enzo Maresca’s patience-first philosophy.

Yet these glimpses of his genius have been fleeting in the Premier League’s most high-pressured matches. In 27 games versus Chelsea’s ‘Big Six’ opponents, Palmer has scored only two non-penalty goals.

Both of those arrived against United in his very first season when Mauricio Pochettino got the best out of him.

That is not to disregard the eight penalties he has dispatched which displayed his willingness to embrace extreme psychological pressure from 12 yards.

But statistically, his goals per 90, assists per 90, shots per 90 and chances created per 90 all decrease when playing Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, United or Tottenham Hotspur, compared to his Premier League output overall ever since signing for Chelsea in 2023.

He has had a fun time toying with Spurs on occasion, but not last weekend. Palmer was deservedly shown two yellows in that 2-0 defeat, Chelsea’s first home loss to their rivals since 2018 – one for barging into Mateus Fernandes, and the other for standing on Conor Gallagher’s ankle.

We get it – he was frustrated, feeding on scraps, hardly ever in the game. But this was a flashback to the ill-discipline which plagued Chelsea’s previous campaign under Maresca.

In the 2025 Club World Cup final, Palmer made Paris Saint-Germain’s superstars seem mediocre compared to him

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Chelsea need Palmer to step up now that he is back from his ban

There was nothing cool to that performance from a player who now sells his own ice cubes – it's £3.50 for four pieces shaped like footballs if interested – and Alonso privately reminded him afterwards about the importance of emotional control. Palmer apologised.

It was the first red card of his career, and the first shown to a Chelsea player since Alonso took charge in the summer, with Palmer suspended for their Carabao Cup penalty shootout loss to Liverpool on Wednesday. Another opportunity at a trophy slipped away at Anfield.

With Joao Pedro sidelined – and no specific date set for his return from a knee injury – Chelsea need Palmer to step up now that he is back from his ban.

Against the United team that a fair few thought he could be joining in the summer would be as good a time as any to repay Chelsea’s faith and begin banishing the ‘Big Six’ narrative attached to his name.

Aston Villa have decided to launch legal action against Jamie Carragher in a row over his comments about Unai Emery
