#1416. Falkirk boss John McGlynn backs Scott Bain to be Scotland's No 1 after 'game of his life' against Celtic

Published: 14:59 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 14:59 EDT, 1 November 2026

Falkirk manager John McGlynn has backed goalkeeper Scott Bain to establish himself as Scotland's No1 between the sticks after producing the 'game of his life' to earn his side a stunning 2-0 win over Celtic.

Bain has been in top form this season, and was at his very best once again as he pulled off a string of outstanding stops to keep the defending champions at bay, with Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser finding the net for Falkirk at the other end.

The 34-year-old was called into new national team boss Sebastien Pocognoli's squad for the recent Nations League quadruple-header, but had to settle for a place on the bench, with Angus Gunn given the nod.

But McGlynn believes the former Celtic shot-stopper has done more than enough to earn an opportunity to add to his four Scotland caps when the next round of international fixtures comes around later this month.

He said: 'I don't want to take anything away from the outfield players but Scott Bain had the game of his life.

'I've been pushing Scotty for a while because I know how good and calm and good with his feet he is.

Scott Bain acknowledges the Falkirk supporters after his stunning display against Celtic

Falkirk boss John McGlynn says keeper Bain had the 'game of his life' in their 2-0 victory

Bain pulls off one of several fine saves by turning Haissem Hassan's shot round the post

'Everything you want he'll deliver. Wherever you are, he can't go unnoticed. He could easily be doing a job for Celtic but I'm delighted we've got him and he's producing the goods which can only help us going forwards.'

McGlynn was delighted with his side's overall display which delivered a fourth Premiership victory on the bounce.

The Bairns are now up to fourth in the table, and have the chance to leapfrog Hearts next weekend when they take the trip to Tynecastle.

'Huge credit to my players,' he said. 'It was a remarkable shift.

'It was a great start. To get a goal so early is beyond your wildest dreams because you're usually chasing the game.

'We defended well and defended set plays and he [Bain] was there to save or punch.

'There was [good] football in there. It was a great second goal and Scotty [Tanser] hasn't been in the mix and hasn't played a lot.

'For him to come in and have the calmness to slot it away... I'm delighted. There's a great opportunity for him on that side.

'Huge compliments to every player. The subs had to go on and continue what the players had been doing which was working really hard and they did that.

'Four wins on the bounce, three clean sheets in a row. Ecstatic.

'The boys have been doing great in these weeks. We've had some sore ones losing late goals.

'There's been a togetherness that's taken us to another rung of the ladder and they've gone the extra mile for each other. Today will increase our determination and desire to get better.

'It's been building. There were signs. We've been in every game.

'It's going to give them a huge boost. At the start we had some big fixtures which is difficult when you're putting a team together.

'We had the confidence going into this game and we'll go to Tynecastle with a lot of confidence, [but] Hearts have been exceptional there.'

The win was Falkirk's first in ten fixtures against either half of the Old Firm since their return to the top flight last summer, and the manager admitted he was pleased to finally get the monkey off their back.

'It was one of the boxes left to tick,' he said. 'Thankfully we've done that.

'Last season over 24 points against the Old Firm we got two, when we drew with Rangers twice, so we're already a point better off. Hopefully there are more points to pick up.'

#1415. After Robbie Fowler claimed the moon landing is 'bulls***' and dubious Joe Cole said he has 'questions' for Neil Armstrong... who makes our ultimate XI of football conspiracy theorists?

Published: 02:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:15 EDT, 1 November 2026

Robbie Fowler certainly helped to draw attention to his new podcast with his former Liverpool and England team-mate Steve McManaman this week by airing his views on the 1969 moon landing.

After answering fan questions ranging from favourite films, comedians and useless talents, Fowler responded to McManaman's prompt of the moon landing as a conspiracy theory.

'I think the moon landing is bulls*** to be fair,' with an excited McManaman declaring 'that is a massive one,' before declaring his subsequent reasoning made 'perfect sense'.

He is far from the only footballer to have doubts, with another ex-England international Joe Cole declaring he would like to sit down with Neil Armstrong – who died in 2012 – to get to the bottom of it.

Fowler later quipped he is 'not a flat earther' having been up on a plane. However, some former footballers are, while others have raised a wide range of conspiracies, ranging from the small scale to the more wild.

Here, Daily Mail Sport puts together our ultimate XI of football's conspiracy theorists.

Former Liverpool forward Robbie Fowler admitted this week he believes the moon landing is 'bulls***' Source: YouTube - We'll have a look podcast

For many, David Icke is football's original conspiracy theorist – so entrenched in his off-the-wall beliefs and so willing to share them publicly that he is more widely known as a crackpot than a goalkeeper.

Nevertheless, Icke turned out for Coventry City's youth set-up between the sticks in the late 1960s, and later played for semi-professional outfit Hereford United before hanging up his boots and pivoting to sports journalism.

While his playing career might have been small-fry, his commitment to conspiracy theories is Premier League. Among his often-cited beliefs is the idea that an inter-dimensional race of reptile-like shape-shifters – the 'Babylon Brotherhood' have infiltrated the upper echelons of global society.

Among the accused are the late Queen Mother, the Rockefeller and Rothschild families, and former Prime Minister Edward Heath, whose eyes, Icke alleged, he saw turn 'jet black' when the pair met in 1989.

Icke also believes that the 'Illuminati' at the top of the global food chain organised world events including Dunblane, 9/11, the assassination of John F Kennedy, the death of Princess Diana to prompt their subsequent responses. Less laughable is the thick seam of anti-Semitism which critics believe runs through his thinking, although Icke has denied this.

For many, David Icke is football's original conspiracy theorist, with one of his cited beliefs is the idea that reptile-like shape-shifters have infiltrated the upper echelons of global society

Javi Poves endured a similarly unmemorable professional playing career in Spain, but did at least register one La Liga appearance with Sporting Gijon. Then, he quit. It was a matter of principle: he had grown to believe that 'professional football is only money and corruption'. Not an unreasonable view point, from some perspectives, but years on from his 2011 resignation things become somewhat more surreal.

Poves joined lower-division Madrid club Mostoles Balompie in 2016 and later became the club's president. In 2019, he renamed the club Flat Earth FC, to draw attention to his primary cause.

'Football is the most popular sport and has the most impact worldwide, so creating a club dedicated to the flat earth movement is the best way to have a constant presence in the media,' he said that year.

'Flat Earth FC is the first football club whose followers are united by the most important thing, which is an idea.'

Although Poves has since moved to fellow amateur side CDC Moscardo, he remains passionately committed to the idea that the earth is flat and not round, and other environmentally-rooted conspiracy theories. These include viewing 'chemtrails' as a deployment of toxic chemicals, and refusing to believe that suncream can help prevent skin cancer.

One thread which runs through a number of players included in the XI is a scepticism of Covid-19. Some, like Sol Campbell, have suggested that the pandemic was in some way man-made. Icke is in the camp which believes that the lockdown and vaccination scheme was akin to governmental 'facism'.

Lovren was firmly in team Icke during the lockdown years, posting a number of his videos on social media. He also used social media to attack Microsoft billionaire Bill Gates, implying some kind of conspiracy with his comment: 'Game over Bill. People are not blind' on Gates's online tribute to health workers.

The Croatian defender seemed particularly swayed by Icke's theories around the links between Covid-19 and 5G technology in 'controlling' populations, with Lovren resharing clips with the caption 'we will not be censored'.

Dejan Lovren supported Icke's views during the pandemic and hit out at Bill Gates

Lovren took to Instagram to promote an interview with Icke during the pandemic

As mentioned in Lovren's section, Campbell also had his suspicions during the Covid-19 pandemic. Then managing Southend United, in May 2020, Campbell appeared to suggest that he believed the disease was made deliberately and designed to target certain population groups.

'Was this virus a natural mistake or a designed mistake...?' he posted on social media. 'I wonder does this virus deliberately attacks a certain blood type.....?'

Campbell shared his idea alongside a screenshot of an article citing an ONS report that showed Black people were four times more likely to die from Covid-19 than any other ethnic group. He later was widely derided for having no scientific evidence to support his argument.

Sol Campbell appeared to suggest in 2020 he believed Covid-`9 was made deliberately and designed to target certain population groups

Campbell shared his idea alongside a screenshot of an article citing an ONS report that showed Black people were four times more likely to die from Covid-19 than any other ethnic group

The former Manchester City defender has previously admitted to a conspiracy theory that has more sympathetic readers nodding in approval: he believes in ghosts.

Delph admitted in 2016 that he sees ghosts 'all the time', adding that 'genuinely' he had seen about 'four'.

'When I first signed for (Aston) Villa I stayed in a hotel there was lots of things moving in the room, a lot of bangs,' he told Man City's official YouTube channel.

'And about four months ago I saw, in my house in God's country (Yorkshire), I saw two ghosts in my bedroom.'

'I don't think they're there to harm me. But I've definitely seen them. It was just a split second and then they were gone.

'The one four months ago, that actually was carrying a body, it went out onto my balcony, then disappeared.'

Joe Cole admitted he is open to having his head turnedabout the moon landings and would be keen to sit down with Neil Armstrong to 'get to the bottom of things'

Compared to how some of the other members of Daily Mail Sport's XI have at times risked public safety or aired unpleasant and divisive views, Cole's position on the 1969 Moon Landings feels somewhat milquetoast.

Additionally, unlike many, he admitted that he is open to having his head turned, with Cole keen to sit down with Neil Armstrong, the first man on the moon, to 'get to the bottom' of things.

'I'm not sold either way and I need some convincing. I want to believe it, honestly,' Cole told FourFourTwo. 'But I've heard too much about it being fake - things like the flag waving and the footprints and all the rest of it.

'I would love to sit down with a man who actually went there and be convinced. I want him to tell me exactly how it all went down and some of the science behind my questions.

'I just want to put it to bed. If anyone could convince me, it's the first man to have apparently visited the moon. I don't mind being talked round to new ideas which is why I'd be more than happy for him to tell me how silly I'm being.

'That's what makes you evolve as a human being. You have to be open to different ideas in life.'

If Pove represents a distinctly Spanish-style conspiracy theorist, Marcos Llorente treads the well-beaten path, with his primary focus the benefits of sunlight – to the extent of snubbing suncream – and a suspicion of 'chemtrails'.

Llorente takes his theories on natural light and the sun to the extreme, however. A staunch advocate of the blue light-blocking sunglasses also favoured by stars including Erling Haaland, the Atletico Madrid midfielder also eschews unnatural light sources in his house after dark. Instead, Llorente works on soaking up as much red light as possible.

In the sun, Llorente takes it one step further, frequently sharing incorrect views on suncream's impact on Vitamin D and dismissing the connection between skin cancer and unprotected skin.

Marcos Llorente is a committed wearer of blue light-blocking glasses in a bid to boost his melatonin

Llorente has frequently endorsed the repeatedly debunked theory that 'chemtrails' are the result of government or corporate intervention

Llorente often does so in a tongue-in-cheek way: in April, he dressed up as a bottle of suncream, but with a twist. Written on the bottle in Spanish were messages reading: 'Protect against your biology' and 'Blocking Vitamin D since 1985'.

On the back of the bottle costume in lieu of ingredients, Llorente drew a graph of rising skin cancer rates and an accompanying message.

'Get in the shade when your body tells you, 'That's enough'. Get sun exposure year-round, not just three days in August,' the 'warning label' read. 'Use clothing as sun protection. Start in the morning and work your way up (don't start at 1pm).

'Build melanin gradually. Eat a balanced diet so your skin responds better. Stay hydrated and connect with nature.'

More recently Llorente, a bon viveur and lover of rare steak, 'bulletproof' butter coffee and good wine, has intensified his stance on other medical theories, including alleging that high cholesterol or 'bad' cholesterol does not have an impact on health.

Matt Le Tissier is no single-issue conspiracy theorist, with the Southampton icon borderline indiscriminate about the wide range of his causes.

Like many, his outpourings amplified amid the pandemic, with Le Tissier frequently opining on the efficacy of vaccines and painting 'big pharma' as a bogeyman. Then, in 2022, he was stood down from his role as Saints ambassador after peddling Russian lies that the massacre at Bucha, in Ukraine, had been fabricated. This came despite the fact that there was video, satellite, and photographic evidence that Russia had murdered over 320 people in the town.

Earlier this year, Le Tissier found himself in a spat with Grok, X's AI chatbot, over 'chemtrails', asking: 'Hey (Grok), why do some plane trails disperse quickly while others hang around and spread out to form grey blanket clouds?'

The bot had responded that the contrails lingered or didn't due to atmospheric conditions, much to Le Tissier's displeasure, with the former midfielder grumbling that Grok was 'spouting government propaganda'.

Matt Le Tissier, pictured taking a selfie at a Southampton game in February, has frequently raised conspiracy theories over social media

Former Wales international David Cotterill sparked widespread backlash in 2022 when he referred to 'false flag events' using 'crisis actors' at the whim of 'controllers' within hours of a fatal school shooting in Texas.

Cotterill said in the incendiary post that 'false flag events are one of their go to methods of manipulating the public opinion to bring about change'.

He also alleged: 'America is the last major country that allows it's [sic] citizens to arm themselves. Which they can't really have with what they're planning to do in the coming months and years.'

Cotterill later stressed that the post had not been related to the Texas massacre, instead stating that his post was 'just about recent articles when you see some of the stuff about the pandemic'.

He similarly received intense criticism when he suggested that the retirement of Brighton's 24-year-old Enock Mwepu due to cardiac issues was linked to side effect of the Covid-19 vaccine.

Cotterill remains unrepentant however, recently appearing on a podcast where he admitted that he supports 'everything' Le Tissier says, and revealed his belief in 2016's discredited Pizzagate conspiracy, among other conspiracy theories.

'I've gone into so many rabbit holes. If you see lots of things happening in the world with the number 33, which is obviously massive for Freemasonry and symbolism,' he told Made in Brum Podcast. 'If you see a lot of things that happen in the world, 33 is not far from that. Some people think I'm f***ing nuts.

David Cotterill sparked widespread backlash in 2022 when he referred to 'false flag events' using 'crisis actors' at the whim of 'controllers' within hours of a fatal school shooting in Texas

Former Liverpool and Southampton star Rickie Lambert is among this cohort's Covid-19 conspiracy theorists, starting off on social media as a staunch vaccine sceptic - only to fall deeper into more fringe views.

Unusually, in 2023, Lambert claimed that he believed that one can change the molecular structure of water based on speaking to a glass of the substance positively or negatively.

'The one word where water responds in the most beautiful way, with the most beautiful crystals, is showing gratitude to water,' Lambert said.

More recently, Lambert has been an active supporter of the campaign against '15-minute cities', whose detractors believe is a government scheme to control the movement and rights of people, rather than an attempt to provide walkable goods and services.

Ahead of attending a protest in Liverpool in September 2023, Lambert's call to arms to publicise the event stressed that the scheme was 'a controlled tactic being implemented across this country' and that Merseyside was set to be put under permanent surveillance.

Rickie Lambert has claimed talking positively to water makes it clean

Like Cole, Fowler appears to have merely dipped a toe into the world of conspiratorial thinking, and has similarly alighted on the Moon Landing as the target of his suspicion.

Unlike the former Chelsea star however, there seemed to be little that would change his mind when he discussed the topic with his We'll Have A Look podcast with co-host Steve McManaman.

'I think the Moon Landing is bulls***, to be fair,' Fowler said. 'Because there was a race in the Sixties, between the Americans and the USSR.

'All of a sudden, the USSR were ahead of the Americans (after Yuri Gagarin became the first man in space) and all of a sudden, the Americans got there first.

'I think it's a bit far-fetched. I don't know, that is the general gist of what I'm saying - I just don't think it was real.'

#1413. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Tonight’s hosts are yet to qualify for a major tournament and are expected to set up in a defensive shape. England defender Esme Morgan believes the squad are ready for a long night of breaking down a stubborn opposition.

She told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the plan and being patient.”

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson says. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

“My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1412. Hibs boss insists his improving team are ready to upset the odds against Rangers in cup final

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EDT, 1 November 2026

Marink Reedijk warned Rangers that they'll face an ever-improving Hibs team when they meet in the Premier Sports Cup Final next month.

The Dutchman created history by becoming the first manager of the Easter Road club to taste a Hampden victory over Hearts when they came from behind to win 2-1.

After recording just one draw in his four opening league games, Reedijk was starting to feel the heat ahead of the semi-final.

But having secured a date against Rangers on December 13, the Leith boss feels his side are now in a different place.

Asked what gave him the confidence that his side can now upset the odds and win the cup for the first time since 2007, Reedijk said: 'The performance of today and the performance we showed the week before.

'And if we have more progression, we can make every opponent's lives a little bit difficult or very difficult.

Hibs boss Marink Reedijk celebrates his team's 2-1 win over Hearts with Josh Mulligan

'And no matter which team it is, it's always another match to play.

'Finals are, again, special matches, but also finals are not only based on these special moments.

'It's also about teams with a plan and teams with an idea.

'And I think if we build on what we are doing now, keep on going - it will have ups and downs - I know I have a really good belief that we also can do something in the final.'

Behind when Claudio Braga struck on four minutes, Hibs responded brilliantly and deservedly went in ahead at the break thanks to goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath.

Reedijk was effusive in his praise for the way his players bounced back from the early blow to dominate the game.

'In the first half, I really enjoyed how we played football, how we dominated the game on the ball, how we made sure that we created chances and gave Hearts a big problem in defence,' he reflected.

'And in the second half, I really enjoyed the togetherness, the work rate, the energy, the desire.

The Hibs players start the party after reaching League Cup final by beating Hearts

'This is where we made a big step today. And also I'm so happy for the staff, the players, because they worked so hard for this. And that's really important.

'Not only those people, like the staff and the players, but also for the fans who kept on supporting us, not only during the match, but especially those matches where we didn't have the result like it was today. And that's really important to me.

Reedijk was asked if his first victory at the fifth attempt was the first real sign that the players had bought into what he was trying to do.

'Not the first sign,' he stressed. 'For me, I already saw glimpses and signs in the last matches, starting at Falkirk, where you see that we dominated the game, but we didn't bring the game home and lost by individual errors and moments.

'And then against Celtic and St Mirren also you saw that we can dominate matches, that we can make our way of playing a challenge for the opponent. That didn't lead to the result we wanted.

'However, today it did. So, it is not the first sign, but it is the first performance with a result.'

Jamie McGrath soaks up the acclaim after putting Hibernian in front at Hampden

At full time, the entire Hibs squad lapped up the rendition of Sunshine on Leith which was sung by their supporters.

Reedijk admitted that he felt more emotional at the scenes than his impassive demeanour suggested.

'I'm not always showing my emotions, but it's really touching,' he said.

'Maybe it looks like I'm an ice king, so to say.

'Normally in Holland we say ice queen, but therefore an ice king because I'm not a woman.

'But for me, it is really important that this happens and it comes close to my heart because this is what football is about.

'Guys who inspire people on the pitch with something people off the pitch and in the stands love to see.

#1411. Branthwaite Fitness Update Ahead Of Second Newcastle Clash

Jarrad Branthwaite is expected to be available for Everton's Premier League clash with Newcastle United on Monday evening (8pm GMT kick-off).

The England defender has been absent from the Blues' past two games due to concussion protocols, after a clash with Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez nearly a fortnight ago.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference, which took place immediately after the Blues' 3-1 win over Newcastle in the Carabao Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday night, Moyes said: "Jarrad should have recovered from his concussion and also the timescale which we had to abide by."

Asked if the Toffees came through the Carabao Cup tie without any further injury concerns, he added: "I think so. I know we're talking about Monday, but you never know until you get them back in the following day [after the game] and see how everybody is – but hopefully things will be okay."

#1410. Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken says the loss of two more players to injury was costly in semi-final defeat

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:31 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EDT, 1 November 2026

Wouter Vrancken claimed Hearts were unable to cope with the double blow of losing Tomas Magnusson and Calvin Miller as their hopes of lifting the Premier Sports Cup ended with a 2-1 defeat by Hibs.

Already missing eight first-team players, the Tynecastle men were further depleted when the pair left the field inside the opening 38 minutes of their semi-final at Hampden.

Vrancken felt the loss of two more key players was instrumental in his side failing to build on the early lead handed to them by Claudio Braga.

Instead, Hibs hit back with goals by Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath to secure a place in next month's final against Rangers.

'I'm really sore and disappointed, of course, especially when you see how the game was going,' said Vrancken.

'It didn't have to go that way because we had control with how we started.

Wouter Vrancken insists Hearts had control until two key players left the field with injuries

Tomas Magnusson is treated for a head knock that led to his substitution early in the semi-final

Calvin Miller uses crutches after going off with what appeared to be a knee injury at Hampden

'But it changed the moment Tomas was injured, that's clear. And then afterwards with Cal.

'I'm not pointing out the guys who came out, but those changes took us out of our rhythm.

'We lost some connections and weren't top in the duels. At first, we were picking up second balls and finding the right spaces.

'But then we lost those profiles and we were searching again. There were hesitations and that gave Hibs too much space.

'You lose the game in that 20 minutes. At half-time, we tried to make adjustments, be clear and try to take those hesitations out.

'It was much better and we dominated the game again.

'Unfortunately, we didn't get rewarded. The players have taken a lot of knocks mentally and emotionally so you just hope they get rewarded for fighting hard.

'It's a pity they didn't especially in such a game.'

Magnusson came off with a head-knock while Miller succumbed to what appeared to be a knee injury.

'I haven't seen Tomas because he's at hospital,' Vrancken explained.

'Calvin is in a brace, but it's difficult to say. We have to wait for a scan tomorrow.

'With Tomas, the medical staff did a concussion test on the pitch at that moment.

'He passed it but when he came to me, he was going from left to right and couldn't stand on his legs any more.

'When I saw that, there was no doubt in my head about letting him back on the pitch. He said, I can't do it.'

Vrancken now faces serious selection issues for the Conference League match away to Swiss side Thun on Thursday.

'I don't know how I make changes. We'll see how it goes and who's fit,' he said.

'Players will have to play out of position, so we'll see who has the quality to play in certain ones.

'We have to make the puzzle on Monday or Tuesday.

'And we have to keep pushing the guys because when you go on the pitch, there can be no excuses, you have to take responsibility, go for it and try to win the game.

'We have 10 out. When you have those 10, you have a really good squad in the Premiership.

'The players have taken responsibility in difficult moments, like dominating parts of the game today.

'When they do that, you just hope they reward themselves like they did today in the second half. It's just a pity the last 20 minutes of the first half which killed the game.

'Everyone is disappointed, no matter the situation we're in.

'When you see the second half, you know there was something in the game today even with the knocks we got.

'So, the disappointment is really big, not about losing players, but missing the chance to beat your rivals and go to the final.'

#1409. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not issue Richardson with a caution.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

“LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel)

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1407. Bradley Lowery's mum issues heartbreaking statement to condemn 'cruel' Coventry fan who used her late son's photo to taunt Sunderland fans as 14-year-old boy hands himself into police

Published: 10:02 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EDT, 1 November 2026

Bradley Lowery's mum has released a heartbreaking statement after a Coventry fan appeared to use his photograph to taunt Sunderland supporters.

The deplorable behaviour came during the Premier League clash between the two sides on Saturday, which the Sky Blues won 3-1.

A video on social media showed a supporter holding up a picture of Bradley - who tragically died from a rare form of childhood cancer at the age of six in 2017 - smiling in the direction of Sunderland fans, with the individual pointing at it and seen smirking at the same time.

A 14-year-old boy 'handed himself in' to West Midlands Police on Sunday.

In a statement on Sunday morning after the behaviour of the Coventry fan went viral, Bradley's mum Gemma shared a heartbreaking message.

'My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate,' she wrote. 'Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

A Coventry fan appeared to use a photograph of Bradley Lowery to taunt Sunderland fans

A fan held up a photo of Bradley, the Sunderland fan who tragically passed away aged six from a rare form of childhood cancer, and was seen smirking and pointing

'I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

'We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter? I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were.

'I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this. Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.'

Gemma continued: 'What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did. Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

'Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever. That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.

'So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents. My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours.'

Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, and formed a touching relationship with then Sunderland striker Jermain Defoe

Confirming that a teenager had handed himself in to authorities on Sunday, West Midlands Police said in a statement: 'We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City's Premier League match with Sunderland.

'A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course.

'We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim's family, and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.'

Coventry condemned the shameful behaviour in a strongly-worded statement on Saturday.

It read: 'Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

'The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.'

Since Saturday's clash, more than £1,000 has been donated to the The Bradley Lowery Foundation by Coventry City fans, with many supporters leaving heartfelt messages as they refused to let the actions of one person define them.

Bradley was previously used by a fan as a taunt back in 2023 when Sheffield Wednesday supporter Dale Houghton was seen holding up a picture of him at a match against Sunderland and laughing.

Houghton was subsequently handed a 12-week suspended prison sentence and ordered to do 200 hours unpaid work.

Bradley pictured with his mum Gemma at his sixth birthday party back in May 2017

Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, before he tragically passed away aged just six in 2017.

The Bradley Lowery Foundation was set up in his honour, with the charity aiming to help families who are fundraising for treatment or equipment that is not readily available or covered by the NHS, while it also supports research into various childhood cancers, including neuroblastoma.

Bradley, who was diagnosed with neuroblastoma when he was just 18 months old, also built up a touching relationship with Jermain Defoe, who later called him his 'best mate'.

Defoe played for Sunderland at the time, and speaking in 2023, he said: 'He will always be in my heart, for the rest of my life. There's not a day that goes past where I don't wake up and think about little Bradley, because his love is genuine.'

#1405. Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock reveals he hid seizures from club because he was 'petrified' of being released as youngster

Published: 19:09 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EDT, 1 November 2026

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock has revealed he hid seizures from the club out of fear that the Reds would axe him.

Warnock, 44, played 67 times for Liverpool and has transitioned into broadcasting since retiring from playing in 2018.

He suffered from a number of epileptic fits as a youngster - a condition that affects around one in every 100 people.

Warnock never understood what was causing his seizures and told 5 Live: 'I was petrified of telling Liverpool because I was worried about being released. Because I was thinking "if they think I've got a condition they will release me".

'I was worried about being on the pitch and it happens. There were no triggers for me, I never knew what triggered it. That was what petrified me.'

Warnock experienced the seizures for around three years and underwent a number of tests including a CT and MRI scan.

Stephen Warnock, pictured working as a broadcaster, revealed he suffered from seizures

The former Liverpool defender, pictured in action for the Reds back in 2005, said he was terrified of telling the club about his health issue

'I was at a computer and then I woke up in a hospital bed,' he went on. 'And I was like "wow, how have I got here?". I didn't remember anything, I completely blacked out.

'My friends told me I started having a seizure. Obviously an ambulance was called and I was taken to a hospital bed.

'I was embarrassed to be honest, because no-one else had it, no-one knew about it, I didn't know about it until it happened.'

The risk of having a seizure can be reduced with medication and Warnock has not experienced one since he was 14.

'I was in a fortunate position where I grew out of it,' he said.

'I didn't have to go on medication or worry about driving a car or things like that. It's the first time I've ever really spoken about it.'

Warnock, a left-back, departed Liverpool in 2007 and went on to play for Aston Villa, Leeds and Derby among other sides.

He has appeared on a number of television channels while working as a pundit, including the BBC, Sky Sports, BT Sport, NBC and DAZN.

#1404. Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

Liverpool have not held talks about bringing Trent Alexander-Arnold back to Anfield, with Fabrizio Romano making it clear that neither the defender nor Real Madrid are currently planning a January separation.

The 28-year-old has endured a difficult spell in Spain and has struggled to reproduce the influence he had at Liverpool.

Injury problems affected his first season at the Bernabéu, while he is now competing with Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries for minutes under José Mourinho.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Romano directly addressed the growing speculation surrounding a potential Liverpool reunion.

He said: “The reality, guys, behind the scenes is quite different.

“First of all, let me clarify links between Trent and Liverpool for a potential comeback are completely out of mark in the sense that Liverpool never started any kind of concrete or serious conversation to bring Trent Alexander-Arnold back to the club. First point.

“Second point. In general, about Trent Alexander-Arnold returning to the Premier League or leaving Real Madrid in any case – that’s not something that Trent is planning for the January transfer window or Real Madrid either.

“So, at the moment, Trent and Real Madrid plan to continue together at least, at least until the end of the season.

“And in reality, the feeling from both sides is that they want to continue together for the long term.”

Romano’s update strongly contradicts recent suggestions that Liverpool could be positioning themselves to re-sign their former academy star.

A related CaughtOffside report also stated that Alexander-Arnold remains focused on proving himself in Madrid rather than immediately seeking an escape route.

The links are easy to understand. Alexander-Arnold spent almost his entire career at Liverpool before moving to Madrid, and his passing range and creativity remain qualities the Reds could use.

But there is a major difference between an emotional reunion making sense on paper and Liverpool actually working on a deal.

Romano’s information suggests there is currently no serious movement whatsoever.

That also makes sense from Alexander-Arnold’s perspective. Leaving after such a short period would effectively mean admitting his Real Madrid move had failed, something he is unlikely to do while he still believes he can win Mourinho’s trust.

Liverpool have also developed other options on the right side of defence, meaning any return would need to make tactical and financial sense rather than simply appeal to nostalgia.

For now, Alexander-Arnold appears determined to stay and fight.

Unless his playing time remains limited deep into 2027, talk of a Liverpool comeback looks more like speculation than an active transfer possibility.

Kai Havertz made Premier League history in the perfect setting, scoring Arsenal’s winning goal at Anfield while becoming the highest-scoring German player the competition has ever seen.

The 27-year-old struck after just 16 minutes to secure Arsenal’s 1-0 victory over Liverpool, ending the Gunners’ 14-year wait for a Premier League win at Anfield.

More significantly on a personal level, the goal took Havertz to 46 Premier League strikes, moving him clear of former Manchester City midfielder İlkay Gündoğan.

Havertz’s simple back-post finish made history, with Declan Rice providing the decisive delivery.

Opta confirmed that Havertz is now the Premier League’s all-time leading German goalscorer with 46 goals, surpassing Gündoğan’s previous record of 45.

Of those goals, 19 came during his time at Chelsea and 27 have now been scored for Arsenal. His Anfield winner was also his third Premier League goal of the current season.

Kai Havertz is now the top German-scorer in Premier League history 😤🇩🇪 https://t.co/lWpXBt0sI5

— Prime Video Sport UK (@primevideosport) November 1, 2026

The occasion made the record even more memorable. Arsenal had not won a league game at Anfield since September 2012, but Havertz’s early finish proved enough to send Mikel Arteta’s side back to the top of the Premier League, three points ahead of Manchester City.

Arsenal punished Alisson Becker’s costly distribution error before Havertz finished the move.

Kai Havertz gives Arsenal an early lead at Anfield! ⚡️ https://t.co/eeyhRcLlel

— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 1, 2026

Havertz’s Arsenal career has often been debated, but milestones like this show just how productive he has become.

He is not always the most spectacular forward, and his finishing can still frustrate, but 46 Premier League goals is a major achievement considering he has spent significant periods playing in midfield rather than as a conventional striker.

Arteta selected Havertz ahead of Viktor Gyökeres for one of Arsenal’s biggest away games of the season, and he repaid that faith with the decisive moment.

Breaking Gündoğan’s record at Anfield while ending Arsenal’s long winless run there makes the achievement even more significant.

Havertz may still divide opinion, but statistically he now stands above every other German goalscorer in Premier League history and at 27, he has plenty of time to extend that record further.

#1400. Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9

“I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

Liverpool needed Barcola to deliver as much as the player himself needed to prove a little point and there is absolutely nothing wrong with having a cause to light a fire. Like a batsman who has been waiting nervously to get off the mark, soon the France international began playing his shots.

A brilliant night should have been glossed by Koumas’s first European goal – he matched Steven Gerrard in becoming just the second player aged 21 and under to assist and score for Liverpool in a Champions League game – but LASK kept pushing and exploited spaces to halve the deficit with a double from Florian Flecker, much to Alisson Becker’s obvious disgust.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

One novice who certainly deserves his starting spot is Trey Nyoni, the England Under-21 international has impressed in the opportunities he has been given so far this year. Watch out for his calmness on the ball and the efficiency with which he uses it.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola said: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

“They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Munoz, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Sonni-Lambie, Lucky

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1399. Invincibles beware! Mikel Arteta might just be assembling Arsenal's greatest EVER defence, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 21:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 03:48 EDT, 2 November 2026

Within seconds of the full-time whistle, Gabriel Heinze had lifted an elated Mikel Arteta off the turf.

The Argentine knew why this result brought his colleague a certain catharsis, which had eluded him for over a decade.

Arteta had previously opened up about the psychological difficulties of playing at Anfield, describing the experience akin to a cyclist suddenly running out of energy. A mental paralysis of sorts.

The game in question was in February 2014, having experienced a 5-1 defeat as a Gunners player. Arsenal’s previous victory against Liverpool away dated back to September 2012, a 14-year wait to banish these demons which he was duly reminded of in Friday’s press conference and in the minutes before kick-off.

Instead, it’s now getting scary for Arsenal’s Premier League title rivals. The prospect of Arteta's side opening up a gap from the chasing pack by Christmas is becoming a real possibility — and it’s all because of their defence.

A William Saliba-less backline reducing the Reds to zero shots on target at Anfield is a moment worth digesting.

Mikel Arteta and Gabriel Heinze jubilantly embrace as the final whistle blows at Anfield

Arsenal ended their 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at Anfield with a superb display

Winning on opposition territory after an abysmal record lasting over a decade is an achievement in itself. But to ensure a frontline featuring Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola aren't given so much as a sniff in front of goal is a further statement.

For all the focus around the fragilities of their frontline — the weaknesses are still very much in the open, as seen by the shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town — it’s Arsenal’s defence which underpins everything.

Since the start of last season, Arsenal have not lost a league game when leading the scoreline at half-time. Just like how Arsenal’s (previously) woeful record at Anfield would be used as a reminder, this statistic is a menacing one for future opponents.

It raises the question: how does this backline compare to the best Premier League defences who came before them?

If the team carry on in this vein towards a consecutive league title, the Arsenal Invincibles set-up from the historic 2003-04 season of Sol Campbell, Kolo Toure, Ashley Cole and Lauren, with Jens Lehmann in goal, could soon be superseded.

The current collection of defenders, backed up by David Raya, create a defensive structure which is proving so hard to break down, even with the lack of a sole regular scorer in the side.

Gabriel, despite his embarrassing attempt at pretending Isak struck him in the face yesterday, stayed strong in physical duels and didn’t relent in periods when Liverpool piled the pressure on.

By the 42nd minute, the Reds had whipped in 17 crosses, many of which were cleared by Gabriel or Konsa.

Riccardo Calafiori is a wonderfully-gifted footballer who finds himself in some unorthodox positions which are difficult to track. The Italian’s menacing runs inverting from the left flank caused Liverpool many a problem.

Kai Havertz tapped home from a low cross early on to give Arsenal a crucial lead to defend

Even Jurrien Timber, who didn’t have his best game in the final third, helped ensure solidity at right back up against Cody Gakpo.

It’s Ezri Konsa, though, who reflects a shrewdness typifying Arsenal and Arteta. As soon as it emerged that Saliba would be sidelined for months with a back injury, a right-sided centre back became the priority.

The 29-year-old has slotted in seamlessly and again shone against the Reds, mirroring the ‘blessed’ tattoo he has inscribed on his left hand.

The versatile defender won 100 per cent of his ground duels, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances. He ranked No1 in all these categories yesterday.

An Arteta team starts from a rock-solid base with multiple, versatile defenders, often at the cost of fewer frontline options (Arsenal struck just two more league goals than third-placed Manchester United last season, for example).

It ultimately worked in the previous campaign, their defence propelling Arsenal to a first Premier League title in 22 years.

Another title appears to be well on track. And: watch out Campbell and Co. The moniker for Arsenal’s best defence in modern history is at risk.

GUNNERS GAINING FROM MIKEL'S RUTHLESS STREAK

Arteta’s ruthlessness is well-documented. Just ask Aaron Ramsdale or Jakub Kiwior, who were eased out after being surplus to requirements in recent years.

Or the cold treatment of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Mesut Ozil earlier in the Spaniard’s reign over their behaviours.

Arteta's ruthlessness with team selection is continuing to pay dividends for the Gunners

The current squad is brimming with talent — and spades of uncertainty.

Eberechi Eze performed well off the bench against Bayern Munich after Bukayo Saka’s thigh injury on 10 minutes, followed up by a start against Everton — and didn’t get a minute against Liverpool.

While Viktor Gyokeres was given his first league start of the season against Everton, where he played well — only to be dropped for this match.

As seen by Christos Tzolis’ dash to make yesterday’s squad ahead of schedule, influenced by Max Dowman’s three-match suspension, no one’s place is really secure.

That makes for a truly competitive environment.

The fiery serial-winner, drafted in by Arteta in July 2025, was always going to demand high standards and bring a ferocity which can turn some the wrong way. At Argentine side Newell’s Old Boys, for example, he would weigh the players twice a day.

Heinze's arrival in July 2025 has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades

So the appointment was attached with risks, even if Arteta had grown close to his ex-team-mate from his Paris Saint-Germain.

It’s turned out to be a clever addition, which has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades.

Sources say that Heinze, who has managed five teams, is well-respected by the players, but is also seen as someone who does not mince his words. They know he’s not here to mess around.

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has delivered a surprising verdict on Trent Alexander-Arnold’s potential return to Anfield, admitting that he is unsure whether re-signing the defender would be the right decision for Andoni Iraola’s squad.

The former Liverpool captain believes Alexander-Arnold possesses the quality to improve the Reds, but has questioned whether bringing him back would benefit the current group following his controversial departure to Real Madrid.

Alexander-Arnold has been linked with a sensational return to Merseyside after struggling to establish himself as a regular starter at the Santiago Bernabéu.

However, Gerrard believes the circumstances surrounding the England international’s departure could complicate any potential reunion.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Gerrard was asked directly whether he would welcome Trent Alexander-Arnold back to Liverpool.

The former Reds captain admitted that he would personally support the move, pointing towards the defender’s exceptional ability and achievements at Anfield.

However, he also acknowledged that the manner of Alexander-Arnold’s departure remains a sensitive subject.

“Ability and talent-wise, the success he’s had, I would say yes. But the ending and that still being a bit raw. I would, yes, myself personally, so I won’t sit on the fence because that’s poor from me.

The 28-year-old left Liverpool after spending his entire senior career at Anfield, having progressed through the club’s academy to become one of its most influential players.

His departure proved controversial among Liverpool supporters, particularly given the manner of his exit that left a sour taste among the fanbase.

Alexander-Arnold’s creativity, passing range and ability to dictate play from right-back would undoubtedly offer improve Liverpool’s right side, specially given that they currently do not have a top-class right-back.

Ronald Araujo has done a remarkable job filling in as a right-back since joining the club on loan from Barcelona but his strongest position remains a centre-back.

And despite Gerrard’s claims, him returning may not have an impact on the dressing room as many players who played with him during his time at the club will likely welcome him back.

That said, the supporters may not be as forgiving, with many on social media already against the idea of bringing him back regardless of the quality he brings.
